The fix in [opencode-copilot-auth#10](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode-copilot-auth/pull/10) only checks if the **last message role** is `assistant` or `tool`. This is incomplete - it still charges premium requests for synthetic user messages like tool attachments (`Tool read_file returned an attachment:`) and compactions (`What did we do so far?`).

I've opened [#8721](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/8721) with a more comprehensive fix for the built-in Copilot plugin in this repo. It detects agent-initiated requests via:

1. **Any** assistant/tool message in history → agent
2. Multiple user messages → agent (multi-turn)
3. Synthetic content pattern matching → agent

This ensures only the initial user prompt consumes a premium request, not follow-up tool calls or synthetic messages.

To clarify - my PR [#8721](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/8721) specifically addresses the `X-Initiator` header detection logic.

The current code only checks `last.role !== "user"`, which fails when:
- Tool attachments inject synthetic user messages (`Tool read_file returned an attachment:`)
- Compaction creates synthetic messages (`What did we do so far?`)
- Subtasks inject user-role messages

These all have `role: "user"` but are agent-initiated, so `X-Initiator` should be `agent` (no premium charge). The fix adds pattern matching to detect these synthetic messages and correctly set the header.

This is orthogonal to the guidance-in-tool-outputs approach you mentioned - both could work together.

1. If ANY assistant/tool message exists → `X-Initiator: agent`
